fish_subjective.name: FishBase BodyShapeI categorical body-shape class
fish_subjective.source: FishBase SPECIES table, field BodyShapeI (elongated / fusiform-normal / short and-or deep / eel-like)
fish_subjective.dataset_class: F categorical trait derived from shape
fish_subjective.status: in hand (cached); never compared with the engine
fish_subjective.prediction: ordinal class predicted from locked BDmax/SL with thresholds fitted on training species only; accuracy above the majority-class baseline (43% 'elongated') within 50 Myr
fish_subjective.reasoning: coarse 3-4 level class; the BDmax error of 0.038 within 50 Myr is far smaller than the class width (~0.1 BDmax/SL); FishBase classes are inconsistently assigned, which caps accuracy

fish_subjective.name: FishBase caudal-fin aspect ratio (SWIMMING table)
fish_subjective.dataset_class: G trait outside the landmark set (negative control)
fish_subjective.status: in hand (cached); 109 target species, 21 within 50 Myr
fish_subjective.prediction: NO skill: the 17-landmark set has no caudal-fin landmarks, so the engine should not beat the consensus on aspect ratio (ratio >= 0.9)
fish_subjective.reasoning: peduncle depth (LM5-LM6) correlates weakly with fin aspect ratio across teleosts, so some incidental skill is possible; n is tiny

other_groups.phylogeny: Economo EP et al. 2018 Nat Commun 9:1778 (species-level tree, ~14,000 tips, grafted)
other_groups.traits: GlobalAnts (Parr CL et al. 2017 Insect Conserv Divers 10:5-20): worker head width, head length, Weber's length, eye length, scape and femur length
other_groups.blind_design: train on species with records in the first GlobalAnts release; predict species added in later releases or in AntWeb specimen measurements
other_groups.reasoning: worker size and Weber's length are strongly phylogenetically conserved in ants; caste polymorphism (majors/minors) and inconsistent measurement protocols add noise; in-hand Camponotus GM data (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18807285) and Pheidole images in .thompson_cache/antscan offer a small first test

other_groups.phylogeny: Kawahara AY et al. 2023 Nat Ecol Evol (2,244 species, time-calibrated)
other_groups.traits: LepTraits 1.0 (Shirey V et al. 2022 Sci Data 9:382): wingspan / forewing length for 12,448 species
other_groups.blind_design: the 2,244 tree species are a small fraction of LepTraits; train on half the tree species, predict the other half, then predict species added to the tree by later studies
other_groups.reasoning: wing size has high phylogenetic signal; LepTraits values are literature-compiled ranges (noisy); essentially a one-trait test of the machinery

other_groups.phylogeny: Houle D, Bolstad GH, van der Linde K, Hansen TF 2017 Nature 548:447-450 (111 species, ~40 Myr)
other_groups.traits: wing landmarks / semilandmarks for the same 111 species (Houle et al. 2017 supplementary data)
other_groups.blind_design: leave-clade-out within the 111 species; a truly blind test needs new species digitised to the same scheme
other_groups.reasoning: closest analogue to the fish engine (2-D landmarks on a time tree) and the dataset where a Thompson-style low-dimensional mode set is most likely to work; small n limits power, hence the lower probability

other_groups.phylogeny: Jetz W et al. 2012 Nature 491:444 (9,993 species; birdtree.org)
other_groups.traits: AVONET (Tobias JA et al. 2022 Ecol Lett 25:581-597): 11 linear traits (beak length/width/depth, tarsus, wing, Kipp's distance, tail, mass) for 11,009 species; 3-D beak shape PCs for 2,028 species (Cooney CR et al. 2017 Nature 542:344)
other_groups.blind_design: train the engine on the 2,028 Cooney beak-shape species, predict AVONET beak length/width/depth for the remaining ~9,000 species (independent measurements, independent team)
other_groups.reasoning: best-case group: complete tree, complete trait coverage, museum callipers, lambda ~ 0.9 for most AVONET traits; the beak-shape -> beak-calliper design mirrors the fish landmark -> calliper design exactly

other_groups.phylogeny: Upham NS et al. 2019 PLoS Biol 17:e3000494 (5,911 species)
other_groups.traits: PanTHERIA (Jones KE et al. 2009 Ecology 90:2648) -> COMBINE (Soria CD et al. 2021 Ecology 102:e03344): body mass, head-body length, and life history; cranial 3-D landmarks for 322 species (Goswami A et al. 2022 Science 378:377)
other_groups.blind_design: train on PanTHERIA (2009) species, predict species whose first measurement appears only in COMBINE (2021): genuinely blind on species not yet measured when the training compilation was made
other_groups.reasoning: body mass is among the most conserved traits known (lambda > 0.95); the two-compilation design gives a clean blind split; COMBINE imputes some values and those must be excluded

other_groups.phylogeny: Tonini JFR et al. 2016 Biol Conserv 204:23 (9,755 species)
other_groups.traits: Meiri S 2018 Glob Ecol Biogeogr 27:1168 'Traits of lizards of the world': maximum SVL, limb/leg state, clutch size, habitat
other_groups.blind_design: train on lizards, predict snakes' SVL? No - different body plan. Train on 2018 release, predict species added in the 2024 update of the same database
other_groups.reasoning: SVL is conserved but repeated limb loss and body elongation across squamates make shape far less predictable than size; a good place to test the horizon rule because the clade is old

other_groups.phylogeny: Jetz W & Pyron RA 2018 Nat Ecol Evol 2:850 (7,238 species)
other_groups.traits: AmphiBIO (Oliveira BF et al. 2017 Sci Data 4:170123): body size, reproductive and ecological traits
other_groups.blind_design: train on AmphiBIO v1, predict species added in later releases
other_groups.reasoning: size conserved at the family level, but miniaturisation is frequent and convergent; the 300 Myr crown implies, under the 0.28 rule, a horizon of ~85 Myr, which is a strong and testable claim

other_groups.phylogeny: Smith SA & Brown JW 2018 Am J Bot 105:302 (seed-plant megatree, ~80,000 tips)
other_groups.traits: Diaz S et al. 2016 Nature 529:167 (six traits: height, seed mass, LMA, leaf area, leaf N, stem density; ~46,000 species) and TRY (Kattge J et al. 2020 Glob Change Biol 26:119)
other_groups.blind_design: train on Diaz et al. 2016 species, predict TRY-only species added after 2016
other_groups.reasoning: seed mass and height have high phylogenetic signal, leaf economics traits much less (lambda ~ 0.5-0.7); plasticity and intraspecific variance are large; the lowest-confidence group on the list

portfolio_hypotheses.statement: For any dataset of linear body-proportion traits on ray-finned fishes (class A), the locked full-30 predictions beat the consensus (ratio < 0.8, paired Wilcoxon p < 0.01) for species within 50 Myr of a training species.
The nearest-relative margin does NOT hold up: on class A fish datasets the full-30 prediction improves on copying the nearest training species by less than 10% (H2-type test fails again).
portfolio_hypotheses.confidence: simulated per dataset below (reported as P(H2 passes); P2 is supported if it does not)

portfolio_hypotheses.statement: Beyond 50 Myr the behaviour is bin-specific, not uniform: the realised BDmax error ratio vs consensus and the realised 95% coverage of each deep-horizon dataset fall inside the simulated intervals given below (ratio +/- 0.10, coverage +/- 10 points). Concretely: cichlids (80-120 Myr) ~0.77 with ~68% coverage; characiforms (>120 Myr, root-state predictions) ~0.43 with ~82% coverage.
portfolio_hypotheses.confidence: subjective 0.6: intervals are simulated, but the tolerance and the transfer across landmark schemes are judgement calls

portfolio_hypotheses.statement: Head-length and predorsal ratios (HL/SL, PD/SL) show weaker skill than BDmax/SL on the same species (error ratio vs consensus at least 0.1 higher).
portfolio_hypotheses.confidence: subjective 0.6: the jaw/head module had a worse process fit than the body module in the engine; FishBase picture measurements of HL are noisy

portfolio_hypotheses.statement: Traits outside the landmark set (caudal-fin aspect ratio) show no skill (ratio vs consensus >= 0.9).

The same machinery (AICc-selected process model on a time tree, Gaussian conditional prediction, horizon-binned calibration) re-trained on another clade beats that clade's consensus within the horizon for every group listed.
portfolio_hypotheses.confidence: subjective, per group (p_beats_consensus); product over groups is the probability all succeed

portfolio_hypotheses.statement: The horizon beyond which 95% coverage collapses below 75% falls at 0.28 +/- 50% of the clade's sampled crown age (fish: 50 of 177.5 Myr) in every group tested.
portfolio_hypotheses.confidence: subjective 0.4: one-point extrapolation; it is registered because it is cheap to falsify

portfolio_hypotheses.statement: Where a Thompson-style low-dimensional a-priori mode set exists (Drosophila wings; bird beaks), it beats the consensus but is worse than the full shape space, as in fish (H6).

subprediction_protocol.step_1: Before downloading or opening a dataset: if its traits are already in the locked registration (BDmax, CPD, HL, PD over SL for all 10,888 Rabosky targets, commit dac08493) nothing new is generated; otherwise generate species-level predictions, SHA-256 them, commit, and publish a preregistration nanopub citing this portfolio nanopub.
subprediction_protocol.step_2: Download; record checksum; match species by exact name; per-species median over specimens/pictures.
subprediction_protocol.step_3: Calibrate the measurement convention with a linear map fitted on TRAINING species only (as in the FishShapes protocol); apply to all methods.
subprediction_protocol.step_4: Score exactly the registered tests (paired one-sided Wilcoxon, alpha = 0.01; tau bins 0-5, 5-10, 10-25, 25-50, 50-80, 80-120, >120 Myr as registered; 95% coverage).
subprediction_protocol.step_5: Publish an outcome nanopub citing the preregistration and this portfolio; update the realised columns of docs/THOMPSON_DATASET_PORTFOLIO.md without changing the registered probabilities.
subprediction_protocol.for_other_clades: Fit the engine on the training split of that clade's tree, lock predictions for every other tip, then obtain the comparison values. Horizon bins are scaled to the clade's crown age.
